subject.title: Add optional `name`/`label` field to group config entries

question: Should OpenClaw add an ignored metadata field to group/channel config entries, and should the durable key be `name`, `label`, or `description`?
rationale: This creates a public config contract across multiple channels, so automation should not invent the field name or scope without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add `name` consistently
options.body: Use `name?: string` as ignored metadata across relevant group/channel entries because it matches the reporter's example and existing account display-name convention.

options.title: Use `label` or `description`
options.body: Choose a more explicitly display-only key, accepting that docs and tooling must distinguish it from runtime channel names.

options.title: Decline metadata for now
options.body: Keep strict behavior-only group entries and instead improve ID discovery or config tooling around existing keys.

recommendation.title: Add `name` consistently
recommendation.body: Use `name?: string` as ignored metadata across relevant group/channel entries because it matches the reporter's example and existing account display-name convention.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history for strict config contracts, shared channel config schemas, and prior review context points to steipete.
